ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
c. The water-air interface has some surface tension, $\sigma$. The effect of surface tension is to change the pressure in the stream according to the Young-Laplace equation,
$$

\Delta P=\sigma\left(\frac{1}{r}+\frac{1}{R}\right)

$$

where $\Delta P$ is the difference in pressure between the stream and the atmosphere and $R$ is the radius of curvature of the vertical profile of the stream, visualized below. ( $R<0$ for the stream of water; the radius of curvature would be positive only if the stream profile curved inwards.)

<image_1>

For this part of the problem, we assume that $|R| \gg|r|$, so that the curvature of the vertical profile of the stream can be ignored. Also assume that water is incompressible.

Accounting for the pressure in the stream, find a new equation relating for $r(y)$ in terms of $\sigma, r_{0}, v_{0}$, and $\rho$, the density of water. You do not need to solve the equation for $r$.

\Delta P=\sigma\left(\frac{1}{r}+\frac{1}{R}\right)

For this part of the problem, assume that $|R| \gg |r|$, so that the curvature of the vertical profile of the stream can be ignored. Also assume that water is incompressible.

method.method_draft: Use an integral Bernoulli-pressure balance between the initial cross-section of radius r0 and speed v0 and a lower cross-section of radius r(y). First read the image as a downward water jet whose vertical side profile has a large radius of curvature |R|; with the text assumption |R| >> |r|, replace the Young-Laplace pressure jump by Delta P(r) ≈ sigma/r. At the reference cross-section, Delta P0 ≈ sigma/r0. Use incompressibility for the axisymmetric stream: pi r^2 v = pi r0^2 v0, so v = v0 r0^2/r^2. Insert this into the Bernoulli relation written with the capillary pressure correction as the pressure-head difference, 1/2 rho v^2 + rho g y = Delta P0 - Delta P(r). method.method_draft: Use a local force/pressure-gradient form and then integrate. From the image, identify the jet as flowing downward and having a vertical profile curvature R that is much larger than the transverse radius; from the text, set the Laplace pressure jump at any section to Delta P(r) ≈ sigma/r. Write the steady one-dimensional mechanical-energy gradient along the stream so that the derivative of kinetic-plus-gravitational head balances the derivative of the capillary pressure jump: d/dy[1/2 rho v(y)^2 + rho g y] = -d/dy[Delta P(r(y))], with the reference capillary pressure Delta P0 = sigma/r0. Integrating from the reference section to y gives 1/2 rho v(y)^2 + rho g y = Delta P0 - Delta P(r). 图像描述：图中灰色区域表示一股水流，水流内部有几根向下的箭头，说明射流向下流动；水流两侧边界是弯曲的，右上侧标出了与竖直轮廓曲率有关的半径 |R|。题目又给定 |R| \gg |r|，因此可以忽略竖直轮廓曲率项，只保留横向半径 r 对 Laplace 压强的贡献。

推理：由 Young-Laplace 方程，在忽略 1/R 后，任意截面的压强差为 \Delta P(r) \approx \sigma/r。参考截面半径为 r_0，因此 \Delta P_0=\sigma/r_0。按照局部压力梯度形式，沿水流的一维稳态机械能梯度满足
\frac{d}{dy}\left[\frac12\rho v(y)^2+\rho g y\right] = -\frac{d}{dy}\Delta P(r(y)).
从参考截面积分到位置 y，得到
\frac12\rho v(y)^2+\rho g y = \Delta P_0-\Delta P(r).
水不可压缩，所以体积流量守恒：\pi r^2 v=\pi r_0^2 v_0，因此
v(y)=v_0\frac{r_0^2}{r(y)^2}.
代入压强差 \Delta P_0-\Delta P(r)=\sigma\left(\frac1{r_0}-\frac1r\right)，得到隐式方程
\frac12\rho v_0^2\frac{r_0^4}{r^4}+\rho g y=\sigma\left(\frac1{r_0}-\frac1r\right).

c. The water-air interface has some surface tension, $\sigma$. The effect of surface tension is to change the pressure in the stream according to the Young-Laplace equation,
$$
\Delta P=\sigma\left(\frac{1}{r}+\frac{1}{R}\right)
$$
where $\Delta P$ is the difference in pressure between the stream and the atmosphere, and $R$ is the radius of curvature of the vertical profile of the stream, visualized below. ($R<0$ for the stream of water; the radius of curvature would be positive only if the stream profile curved inwards.)

For this part of the problem, assume that $|R| \gg |r|$, so that the curvature of the vertical profile of the stream can be ignored. Also assume that water is incompressible.

Accounting for the pressure in the stream, find a new equation for $r(y)$ in terms of $\sigma$, $r_0$, $v_0$, and $\rho$, the density of water. You do not need to solve the equation for $r$.

When |R| \gg |r|, it is approximated as \Delta P(r)\approx \sigma/r; at the initial cross section it is \Delta P_0\approx \sigma/r_0. According to the specified Bernoulli-pressure correction relation, \frac{1}{2}\rho v^2+\rho g y=\Delta P_0-\Delta P(r). Substituting the velocity and pressure difference gives \frac{1}{2}\rho v_0^2 r_0^4/r^4+\rho g y=\sigma(1/r_0-1/r).
